Tom, a civil servant in his mid thirties, is coordinating a workshop with colleagues from several departments. He usually does a quick coffee run beforehand to keep everyone energised. The cafe near the office charges £12 for a box of mixed pastries to go with the drinks.

This month, Tom’s team has been reminded to be extra careful with small discretionary expenses. Looking at the receipts from previous workshops, Tom realises the pastries are nice, but not essential, especially because people often only take one or skip them entirely.

When he checks the café’s menu again, he notices they sell a simple biscuit selection for £4. It’s not as exciting, but it’s still something to have with coffee. Choosing it instead of the pastries saves £8, which fits perfectly with the 'spend wisely' message.

On the day, his colleagues shrug and laugh: Biscuit day today, is it? The workshop goes well, everyone gets what they need, and Tom feels good knowing he made a sensible cut without hurting the atmosphere.
